title: Automating evaluation: test sets and unit tests on output

videos.script: A test set is a list of messages, each with the answer a person decided was right. Every number in this course so far was counted against one. {{title}} This lesson is about the set itself, and about the ways its count can mislead you. {{set}} Each check in the harness is a unit test on one reply. Does it parse, does it have the fields, are the labels legal, does it match the person. The cheap checks run first. {{checks}} Then you meet the easy set. The prompt that passes thirty-six of forty messages its author wrote passes eleven of thirty harder ones, written later. {{holdout}} Next you copy three test messages into the prompt as its examples. The score rises by one, and that one is a message the prompt was shown. {{contamination}} Last, you raise the temperature. The same prompt passes a message on one call and fails it on the next. Two runs of forty disagree by three, with nothing changed. {{flaky}} By the end you can build a set that keeps measuring, and report a number that survives the next run. {{close}}
